18A
Same modern foundation. Different missions.

Both use Intel 18A manufacturing technology, with built-in graphics and dedicated AI engines.

What does that mean? ↗
THE COMMON GROUND

Same family.
A fresh foundation.

18A is how the chip is made.

Think of it as a modern building method. Both families use it for their compute silicon. But the rooms inside—the processing, graphics and AI resources—are sized for different jobs.

Both handle everyday computing. Both can run supported AI features. The difference is how much headroom you need.

18A describes manufacturing technology, not a speed rating. Other chip components can use different processes.
LESS JARGON. MORE “OH, GOT IT.”

Curious about the numbers? Open the tech translation +

CPU = the task team

Up to 16 cores on Core Ultra; up to 6 cores on Core. More cores can help with work that uses them.

GPU = the visual team

Up to 12 Xe cores on Core Ultra; up to 2 Xe cores on Core. Graphics vary significantly by model.

NPU = the AI specialist

Up to 50 NPU TOPS on Core Ultra; up to 17 NPU TOPS on Core. TOPS means trillions of operations per second—not an app speed guarantee.

Family maximums, not every model. Core’s up to 40 platform TOPS includes multiple engines; it must not be compared directly with NPU-only TOPS. Software support, laptop cooling and configuration affect results.
